root_idea.summary: The root centers on attachment or involvement with something, extending to the effort, difficulty, or affectation that such involvement may entail.
root_idea.development: Form I denotes strong attachment or devotion; Form II causatively imposes a task, duty, or burden; and Form V turns effort inward, extending to self-imposed exertion and affected conduct. Related nouns denote difficulty and facial discoloration.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized from the imperfect QAC lemma to the classical Form II perfect citation form كَلَّفَ.
Displayed as the singular active-participle citation form مُتَكَلِّف rather than the Quranic plural مُتَكَلِّفِينَ.

senses.definition: To impose or assign a task, duty, requirement, or burden on someone; in the passive, to be tasked or burdened.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic forms include both active and passive imperfect constructions. With نَفْسٌ and expressions of capacity, the sense concerns the limits of what a person is required to bear or do; passive contexts may accordingly be rendered as being responsible or being burdened. This is one constructional branch, not separate meanings.

senses.definition: One who affects or pretends to possess a quality or manner that is not natural to him; an affected or pretentious person.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural مُتَكَلِّفِينَ in ص 38:86 refers to blameworthy affectation or pretence, rather than merely to commendable effort toward acquiring a quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intensely attached, devoted, addicted, or fond of a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used with بِهِ. كَلَفٌ is its verbal noun and denotes intense or vehement love.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose a difficult task or trouble upon oneself; to put oneself to inconvenience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the reflexive construction كَلَّفَ نَفْسَهُ, distinct from imposing a task on another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To undertake a difficult or troublesome affair, constrain oneself, take pains, or exert forced effort to accomplish it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V may describe a self-imposed task or effort made despite difficulty, trouble, or inconvenience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To endeavor to acquire or display a quality, or to adopt a manner that is forced or not natural; in some uses, to pretend to possess such a quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Classical use includes cultivating or displaying qualities such as courage, using an affected manner in Arabic speech, and straining a point in lexicology. The Quranic nominal use selects the blameworthy affectation branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do something purposely or deliberately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This intentional-action use is attested as the construction تَكَلَّفَ كَذَا.
A specialized idiomatic use with الَقَيْءَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A facial discoloration or dingy redness, including spots or marks resembling sesame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a nominal bodily-condition sense, distinct from كَلَفٌ meaning intense love.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A difficulty, troublesome affair, duty, or obligation imposed on oneself or on another; constraint, trouble, pain, or inconvenience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can denote either a difficult obligation undertaken or a burdensome requirement imposed on someone.

cautions: The Quranic Form II occurrences alternate between active and passive voice; renderings such as “burdened” and “responsible” reflect the construction rather than separate lexical senses.
